34 apartment buildings, Washington DCUpdated Nov 24, 11:36 am ET

Studios and one-bedrooms across 34 DC buildings

Read from each building's own website once a day. Shown: studios, junior and full one-bedrooms of 400 sq ft or more, with base rent of $3,000 or less (the cheapest 12- to 15-month price), and a washer/dryer on the floor plan. Cheapest all-in per square foot first.

Units413 No longer listed8 Buildings34 How it works

Units

Units that pass every filter, and 97 marked "Need a check": they may pass, but something can't be confirmed from the site (no floor plan to look for a washer/dryer, a plan not read yet, a size not posted, or a price over $3,000 at 12 to 15 months with a cheaper one at another lease length), and 9 "Plans only" rows from buildings that post floor plans and "from" prices but not units. Rent before deal is the cheapest 12- to 15-month price the site offers, with its lease length; buildings often charge far more for the one length that would end in a slow month. A deal's total is spread over the lease length and taken off the monthly rent. Where the site doesn't say the deal applies to that unit ("up to", "select homes"), its full value is still in the numbers, marked "deal assumed": ask the leasing office (a lease length that isn't posted is taken as 12 months). Fees are the first year's required fees. All-in a month = rent after deal + required fees (one-time fees spread over the lease length, 12 months where it isn't posted; yearly fees over 12 months) + estimated electricity (incl. heat/AC), water/sewer/trash and internet, each left out where the building covers it + one parking space at the cheapest price the building offers (the average of the buildings found where it isn't posted). Hover it for the parts. Left out: 133 listed units (122 over $3,000; 11 under 400 sq ft).

How it works

  • Each building's own site. Listing sites were wrong on prices by $125 to $450 and on in-unit laundry, so only the building's own pages are read, as a visitor would.
  • One check a day. 8 am Eastern, or within an hour of the laptop waking. A building whose site doesn't answer keeps its last good reading and says when that was; its units are never marked gone by a failed read.
  • Floor plans read once. Closet area, walk-in and island are read from each floor-plan image by an AI model, so closet area is marked est. Checked against 40 floor plans measured by hand at another building: walk-in and island agreed on 39 and 40 of them, and closet area was within 30% on 31. The instructions were tuned on those same plans, so open the plan before relying on a number.
  • Deals. Specials change week to week. Each check records the deal as it stood that day, so history isn't rewritten when a deal changes.
  • What it costs. Nothing per use. Free hosting; floor plans are read on a flat-rate subscription.
  • Who built it. One person set the goals and made the calls. AI agents (Claude Code) built and run it.
Not affiliated with any building. Prices are the buildings' published prices and can change at any time.
